Sports.title: A scary Alexander Isak issue, the punditry duo who outshone struggling Wayne Rooney and who from Man United's 'spine' is still on the beach? IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend
Sports.content:
A scary Alexander Isak issue, the punditry duo who outshone struggling Wayne Rooney and who from Man United's 'spine' is still on the beach? IAN LADYMAN on My Football Weekend

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Without doubt the worst moment of Liverpool's dismal title defence season came when Hugo Ekitike ruptured his Achilles at Anfield against PSG last April. Not only did it rule a talented forward out until 2027, it left Liverpool relying on Alexander Isak this season and that already feels scary.

Watching Isak at St James' Park yesterday was painful. Where once – during his time at Newcastle - there was certainty and instinctive confidence, there is now only hesitancy and doubt.

Isak used to take penalties for his old club but when Liverpool won one in the 96th minute yesterday, I almost hoped he wouldn't take it. He didn't.

But Liverpool need him. They really need him and that already feels like a problem for Andoni Iraola as he tries to navigate the early weeks of his time as Liverpool manager.

As Liverpool laboured in the latter stages against Newcastle, Isak offered absolutely nothing but he stayed on the field simply because Iraola didn't really have any other option.

Alexander Isak must succeed for Liverpool - their early season prospects depend on it

Last summer – the summer of 2025 – saw a number of No 9s arrive at our big clubs. Isak to Liverpool, Benjamin Sesko to Manchester United, Liam Delap to Chelsea and Viktor Gyokeres to Arsenal. None have had it easy so Isak is not alone.

Indeed as the Premier League returned this weekend, none bar Isak started for their teams. Sesko and Gyokeres were on the bench and Delap has been frozen out entirely by new coach Xabi Alonso at Chelsea.

The difference is that United, Arsenal and Chelsea have alternatives. They can afford to start their season with big name strikers as impact players. Iraola and Liverpool do not have that option.

Cody Gakpo – criminally under-rated by some members of the Liverpool fanbase – delivered with a big goal for Liverpool yesterday and could – at a push – play through the middle. Florian Wirtz – who faces challenges of his own at Anfield – could feasibly operate as a false nine. But neither is a convincing alternative.

What Liverpool really need is for Isak to start playing like a £125m centre forward – or indeed any kind of centre forward at all. Currently he looks miles off.

It was never going to be easy returning to St James' Park where even Newcastle manager Matthias Jaissle was whipping up the crowd's vitriol towards a player who once scored 54 Newcastle league goals at more than a goal every other game.

It will feel more straightforward for him when Liverpool host Nottingham Forest at Anfield next Saturday lunchtime.

But at the moment Isak looks like a player who doesn't trust either his body or his mind and that has to change very soon.

Iraola doesn't have the option of asking him to find his form gradually. That was last season's luxury.

It really has to happen now. Liverpool's early season prospects may depend upon it.

Jaissle must look in the mirror

Newcastle coach Jaissle looks as though he will be a lively and entertaining presence on the touchline. But the German was wrong to blame referee Stuart Attwell for the late penalty decision that denied his team victory. The contact from the otherwise excellent Lewis Hall on Liverpool substitute Victor Munoz was clear.

Indeed Jaissle may wish to examine his own part in what happened given that the foul came in time added on by Attwell for a totally unnecessary Newcastle substitution.

Jaissle's decision to replace Yoane Wissa with Fabian Schar in the last minute of added time was clearly designed to waste some precious moments. But all it did was prompt Attwell to add 30 seconds on and it was after 15 of those that Munoz ran at Hall to win the spot-kick.

New guidelines this season mean that players must leave the field within 10 seconds of their number being raised or risk a booking. This means that the classic 'time wasting' substitution is even more pointless than ever.

Is MOTD losing its identity?

It felt strange to see Mark Chapman at Newcastle for Sky the day after he had hosted the season's opening Match of the Day. It is something that chips away a little at the identity of the BBC's flagship show.

TNT, meanwhile, chose to use The Athletic's ace news breaker David Ornstein as one of their pre-match panellists at the Hull-Man Utd game which felt a little like a desperate attempt to jump on the back of his enormous social media following.

As for Wayne Rooney, he continues to struggle to look truly comfortable in the MOTD chair. Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were on this occasion a better combination on the Sunday show than Rooney and Alan Shearer had been 24 hours earlier.

Joe Hart and Danny Murphy were better than Wayne Rooney and Alan Shearer as pundits

A wake-up call for Carrick

Michael Carrick will now know that it really feels like to be a Manchester United manager after his team's lame defeat on Humberside.

Last season was a free hit for Carrick after he succeeded Ruben Amorim as an interim at Old Trafford. Now that he has the job, it is completely different. This is his team and therefore his responsibility.

It was on the one hand hard not to admire Carrick's frankness in his post-match interviews.

When, for example, it was suggested by former Middlesbrough striker Jan Age Fjortoft – now an excellent analyst for foreign rightsholder Viaplay – that his team had lacked 'passion'. Carrick almost bit his head off.

'That is ridiculous,' said Carrick. 'You played football. You [should] understand.'

On the other, Carrick will soon come to learn just how every single word he utters – especially after defeat – will be picked apart by a fanbase that grows ever more impatient for a league title.

For example, he spoke ahead of the Hull game about his team's spine offering him cause for comfort only to see one of the players he name-checked – centre half Harry Maguire – start the season as though he was still on the beach.

The sooner central defenders learn to concentrate on the ball at set pieces the better. When the first Hull goal went in, for example, Maguire was still so intent on holding his man that he actually had both arms wrapped round team-mate Noussair Mazraoui.

It was schoolboy stuff.

Harry Maguire started the season as though he was still on the beach for Man United

Who can be the new Sunderland?

Hull's victory may yet transpire to be a rare highlight in a hard season but it is impossible not to be pleased for a group of supporters who have been through so much since they last watched Premier League football a decade ago.

Indeed both Hull and fellow promoted club Ipswich have followed Sunderland's example of last summer by recruiting heavily to try and repurpose themselves for top-flight football.

Sunderland fielded almost a new team as they flew high last season and a year on Hull have arrived in the Premier League with seven new players – three were in the team that beat United - while Ipswich fielded seven newbies as they beat the Wearsiders at Portman Road.

Ipswich are among the biggest spenders in the Premier League, having shelled out more than £150m. As Sunderland prepare to play European football this season, it seems they may have started something.

Savinho deal doesn't add up

Tottenham have also spent heavily but after their thumping at Brentford it may be a while until we see what they will actually look like under Roberto de Zerbi.

De Zerbi is still without a number of his best players – guys like Dejan Kulusevski, James Maddison, Micky van de Ven and Pedro Porro were not fit to start on Saturday – while one of his anticipated new signings – the Egyptian wide player Omar Marmoush – was actually on the bench for Manchester City yesterday.

So there is much still to come for Spurs fans even if there will be pressure on Tottenham's new executive team for their signings to work out.

Paying Newcastle £100m for Sandro Tonali feels rather top heavy but that pales when compared to the £75m Tottenham have agreed to give City up front for the Brazilian winger Savinho.

The 22-year-old arrived at the Etihad for £30m two summers ago and has made only a modest impact with two Premier League goals and twelve assists.

So who at Tottenham has decided that a 150 per cent increase on value feels like a good deal?

It already feels like one of the strangest transfers in recent Premier League history and if it doesn't work Spurs fans will want answers.

Roberto de Zerbi has seen a number of expensive additions arrive at Tottenham

Arteta spot-on with Martinelli

Arsenal's squad depth is increasingly impressive – the likes of Eberechi Eze, Noni Madueke, Max Dowman, Gyokeres and Martin Zubimendi were all on the bench as the champions beat Coventry – which is why Mikel Arteta feels comfortable in moving on Gabriel Martinelli.

Gunners legend Ian Wright claims Arteta's treatment of the Brazilian has been unnecessarily brutal. Martinelli was not involved at all on Friday or indeed at the Community Shield a week earlier.

But Arteta's track record at ruthlessly shipping players out when they have served their purpose is there for all to see.

The likes of Kieran Tierney, Granit Xhaka and Oleksandr Zinchenko all played significant roles in Arsenal's gradual return to eminence under the Spaniard. Indeed all three captained the club at some stage.

But all were invited to further their career elsewhere once their shelf life was reached. It can feel a little cold-hearted at times. But it has worked for Arsenal and that's what matters.

New hope for England

England assistant manager Anthony Barry – last seen struggling to hold back the tears at half-time of England's World Cup win over France – was on his native Merseyside to watch Everton down wasteful Crystal Palace and there was lots to take in.

A fabulous goal from the talented Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall and an assured display from Adam Wharton will have reminded Barry and his boss Thomas Tuchel that it's possible to do something other than pack an England squad with wingers.

But Barry will also (hopefully) have noted a decent afternoon from talented Everton central defender Jarrad Branthwaite.

The Cumbrian is one of the most naturally gifted centre halves in England but has seen his progress stalled by injury. He is 24 now and it would help England enormously if he stepped up.

Ezri Konsa and new Manchester City 'midfielder' Marc Guehi (what on earth was all that about yesterday?) were very much 6/10 at the World Cup and could do with competition that isn't called Dan Burn.

Glasner needs history lesson

Former Palace manager Oliver Glasner is now at Nottingham Forest and that still feels like an odd swap, given Forest owner Evangelos Marinakis goes through managers like I go through tissues in hay fever season.

After an opening defeat to Leeds at the City Ground, Glasner suggested that it was impossible for him to suddenly make his team play like Real Madrid in the 1970s.

It was a strange thing to say, not least because Real were not winning big European trophies in that era.

A team who were? Forest, of course.

The club's two European Cup wins came in 1979 and 1980.

Oliver Glasner made strange comments about how Nottingham Forest could play

Still too many kid gloves

It was heartening to see a Premier League weekend pass without any notable VAR moments. Long may Howard Webb's 'high bar for intervention' continue. But he said this last season, too, and we know what happened.

Much of the responsibility for change continues to rest with the players, though, and that's particularly the case when it comes to all the messing about at corners and other set pieces.

As we watched Man City goalkeeper Gianluigi Donnarumma wrestle with a Bournemouth player at a corner on the TV in the Newcastle press room yesterday, a voice from the back piped up.

'It's like watching kids in a playground,' she said. It was perfectly put.

Farewell King Kev

Alan Shearer – said to be scaling back his TV schedule this season – was in Newcastle to witness a fabulous and moving tribute to the late Kevin Keegan by two of his former clubs at St James Park.

It really was a super effort by Newcastle and Liverpool and it was fitting that Keegan's family and grandchildren were in the stadium to witness it.

Sometimes football manages to get things very right indeed.

Sports.title: Revealed: Brydon Carse WAS arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly during nightclub visit with Ben Stokes - with police now RE-OPENING investigation into England bowler
Sports.content:
Revealed: Brydon Carse WAS arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly during nightclub visit with Ben Stokes - with police now RE-OPENING investigation into England bowler

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Brydon Carse was briefly arrested on suspicion of being ‘drunk and disorderly’ in Derby on Saturday night, before being de-arrested, it has emerged.

Carse was dropped earlier today from England’s squad for Thursday’s second Test against Pakistan at Lord’s while the Cricket Regulator investigates the events that led to police handcuffing him outside a nightclub.

He was then de-arrested - meaning the arrest was cancelled before he was taken into custody. But Daily Mail Sport understands the matter is now back in the hands of the police, who are looking into the precise sequence of events.

A statement by Derbyshire police read: ‘A man in his 30s was arrested on suspicion of being drunk and disorderly in Derby city centre on Saturday night. However the man was de-arrested shortly afterwards having agreed to leave the area.’

Brydon Carse was handcuffed by police outside the nightclub in Derby

Ben Stokes (in background) was also in attendance after Durham's big win over Derbyshire

Carse has been replaced in the 16-man squad by Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker

It is understood the man in question is 31-year-old Carse, who has been replaced in the 16-man squad by Hampshire fast bowler Sonny Baker.

A social-media video showed the moment Carse was handcuffed, with four policemen in attendance, and Durham team-mates Ben Stokes and Matthew Potts both featuring briefly on camera.

And while Carse, who has not played a Test since last winter's Ashes, was not on England duty, he has an ECB central contract.

After a year in which Harry Brook, Ben Duckett and Stokes have been involved in separate alcohol-related incidents, the sight of another England cricketer making headlines for the wrong reasons has not gone down well at Lord’s.

An ECB statement said: ‘Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the Second Men’s Rothesay Test Match while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained.’

The Cricket Regulator has at is disposal a range of options, including no further action, caution or bringing a charge for a breach of the regulations – among them, bringing the game into disrepute.

Sports.title: Hull City to reward assistant head coach with improved deal... recognising his role in masterminding promotion to Premier League and shock opening-day win over Man United
Sports.content:
Hull City to reward assistant head coach with improved deal... recognising his role in masterminding promotion to Premier League and shock opening-day win over Man United

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Hull City are set to reward assistant head coach Dean Holden with an improved contract following the club’s remarkable start to life in the Premier League.

The Tigers produced one of the biggest opening day shocks in recent Premier League history on Saturday, defeating Manchester United 2-0 at the MKM Stadium.

The victory has further enhanced the reputation of head coach Sergej Jakirovic, who has also agreed a lucrative new deal, reputedly in five minutes after the game on Saturday, on the back of guiding Hull to promotion last season.

But behind the scenes, there is growing recognition that Holden has played a significant role in the transformation of the club.

The former Bristol City and Charlton boss joined Hull in July 2025 as assistant head coach, working alongside Jakirovic. His experience of English football and particular focus on defensive organisation and set pieces have proved invaluable, with Holden quickly earning the respect of both the dressing room and senior figures at the club.

Holden was part of the management structure that masterminded one of the most remarkable seasons in Hull’s recent history, culminating in a 1-0 victory over Middlesbrough in the Championship play-off final at Wembley and promotion to the Premier League.

Hull pulled off one of the shock Premier League results in seeing off Manchester United 2-0

... and now Dean Holden is set to be rewarded with a new, improved contract

His opinion has also been sought beyond the club. Holden appeared on BBC’s Match of the Day following Saturday’s victory, providing an insight into the tactical approach that saw Hull deploy a back five and ultimately overcome United.

Holden’s arrival was part of a wider restructuring of the football operation overseen by former sporting director Jared Dublin, who was instrumental in reshaping the club’s recruitment and football infrastructure before leaving Hull earlier this summer.

Now, with Hull having begun their Premier League adventure in spectacular fashion, owner Acun Ilicali is understood to be keen to ensure Holden is rewarded for his contribution and retained as a key part of Jakirovic’s coaching team.

While Jakirovic has deservedly received much of the credit for Hull’s resurgence, those close to the club regard Holden as one of the unsung heroes behind the scenes and his impending reward is recognition of the increasingly important role he plays in the Tigers’ remarkable story.

Sports.title: Mike Tyson tells Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury to fight on home soil as war of words threatens to derail British showdown
Sports.content:
Mike Tyson has rubbished the idea of Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury fighting in New York and urged the British rivals to clash on home soil – even if it means he is barred from sitting ringside.

After years of trash talk and false dawns, the two British heavyweights looked set to finally meet in a long-awaited showdown later this year.

As reported by the Daily Mail, Joshua and Fury are understood to have signed contracts to fight on November 20 in New York City.

But news that the fight would not be held in Britain sparked a fierce backlash and then on Friday, Fury claimed the fight 'doesn't look like it's going to happen' in an explosive rant at his rival and Joshua's 'money-thirsty' promoter Eddie Hearn.

That does not sit well with 'Iron' Mike, one of the most feared heavyweights in history, who told the Daily Mail that Joshua and Fury must clash on home soil.

'It's going to be a great fight, it's going to be great for boxing… even though I can't go – I'm barred from London – I think London should get the fight,' said Tyson, who is blocked from visiting the UK due to his criminal past.

Tyson Fury has suggested his fight against Anthony Joshua is now unlikely to happen

Fury's explosive rant included barbs at promoter Eddie Hearn and 'coward' Joshua

Mike Tyson has rubbished the idea of Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury fighting in New York

The former heavyweight champion was jailed for rape in 1992 and has also been convicted of assault, cocaine possession and driving under the influence.

'They're both English and if they come here, all the English people are going to come anyway. So you're home already, let's do it there!'

'Everybody that [wants] to be there, they're going to come to the United States – it's going to be full of English people. It's just going to be just like it is over there.

'There ain't going to be many Americans there because they'll sell it out. All the English – very few Americans – sold it out when I fought Frank Bruno [twice in Las Vegas].'

Tyson spoke to the Daily Mail during an event at Sugar Factory in New York's Times Square, where he was promoting new Protein Sliders that he hopes can help people eat more healthily.

The event kicked off just hours after Fury's rant and the 60-year-old remains hopeful that the fight with Joshua will happen.

'It's going to be a great fight, it's going to be great for boxing. And I think they both still have enough in them once they get the desire,' he said.

Fury has fought only twice since he suffered a second consecutive defeat to Oleksandr Usyk in December 2024. After another brief retirement, the 38-year-old has picked up wins over Arslanbek Makhmudov and, most recently, Mariusz Wach.

Joshua, meanwhile, recently returned to the ring for the first time since surviving a car crash that killed two of his closest friends. He beat the unheralded Kristian Prenga, twice climbing off the canvas in round one before securing a second-round knockout.

'People think they lose because they can't fight. They lose because they lose their desire. I'm sure [Joshua] would get back up for this fight. He's had exciting fights, [recently] the guy dropped him, he got back up and he clocked the guy. That was very exciting.'

Joshua beat the unheralded Kristian Prenga, twice climbing off the canvas in round one

Fury publicly called out Joshua to make their fight after his win against Arslanbek Makhmudov

Tyson spoke to the Daily Mail during an event at Sugar Factory in New York, where he was promoting new Protein Sliders

Hearn revealed it was written into 36-year-old Joshua's contract that the fight had to be staged in Britain - only for reports of an agreement to fight at New York's Madison Square Garden to emerge this week.

In a post on Instagram Friday, Fury, 38, said: 'Quick update: Doesn't look like they're going to sign the fight, doesn't look like it's going to happen. All because Eddie Hearn and that want more money.

'They've already had that much money off of Turki in the last few years, Eddie and AJ. They've had boxing deals, darts deals, snooker deals, they've had everything. And yet they've had the audacity and cheek of flea-bitten rats to ask for more money from Turki, who's given you everything combined in the last couple of years.

'You're disgusting, money-thirsty pieces of s***. It is what it is, same old cliche a decade later, keep running you little cowards.'

A Knockout Bite: Mike Tyson Debuts Sugar Factory Protein Sliders... coming soon to ShopRite locations

Sports.title: Transfer news LIVE: Julian Alvarez meeting, announcement imminent, Liverpool and Man Utd latest
Sports.content:
All the latest Premier League and global transfer news, with fresh updates on Arsenal, Manchester United, Liverpool and more.

Andoni Iraola frustrated by a lack of wing options at Liverpool as transfer deadline nears

Welcome to Mirror Football's live transfer blog on Monday, August 24.

Sports.title: Mikel Arteta sets one condition for £130m Julian Alvarez transfer as Arsenal plans emerges
Sports.content:
Mikel Arteta sets one condition for £130m Julian Alvarez transfer as Arsenal plans emerges

Arsenal have spent heavily this summer and a move for Julian Alvarez remains a distinct possibility heading into the final week of the transfer market and Mikel Arteta has now made his stance clear

View 2 Images Alvarez was loudly booed by Atletico Madrid fans over the weekend (Image: Getty Images)

Mikel Arteta is ready to make a £130m push to sign Julian Alvarez - but will demand assurances the Argentina star wants to move to Arsenal.

Atletico Madrid have become embroiled in an ugly stand-off with Alvarez which has seen the club’s own fans turn on the 26-year-old. Alvarez has been pushing for a move to Barcelona but Atletico are refusing to entertain a deal with their La Liga rivals but may now be open to doing business with Arsenal.

The former Manchester City star was booed by Atletico fans during their draw with Villarreal last weekend and there may be no way back for Alvarez.

The World Cup star has previously insisted he only wants Barcelona and clearly Arsenal boss Arteta would need to be convinced the striker would be fully invested in a move to the Emirates.

It would also need Arsenal to be able to balance the books with Brazil winger Gabriel Martinelli closing in on a £50m move to Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal.That would represent a record sale for the Gunners with Martinelli’s initial reluctance to go to Saudi having softened because it is clear that he is no longer central to Arteta’s plans.

Arsenal also want to sell Fabio Vieira with Hamburg pushing to get a deal done while Napoli have been interested in Gabriel Jesus but the biggest stumbling block has been the Brazilian’s wages.

Jesus has also wanted to stay in England but knows his chances at Arsenal will be limited.

View 2 Images Alvarez is keen to push through a move to Barcelona (Image: Getty Images)

It remains to be seen whether Arsenal would even entertain a deal involving Viktor Gyokeres with Atletico Madrid but the chances of signing Juventus star Kenan Yildiz appear remote as the winger needs knee surgery.

Arsenal have already spent big in this window with Christos Tzolis, Bruno Guimarães and Ezri Konsa so it may be a very real possibility they do not do more business even if they sell Martinelli.

They do have Eberechi Eze who can fill on the left flank and may bide their time but if there is a chance of Alvarez and he is willing to move then Arsenal are open.

Sports.title: Brydon Carse dropped from England squad after nightclub incident saw him handcuffed
Sports.content:
Brydon Carse dropped from England squad after nightclub incident saw him handcuffed

England fast bowler Brydon Carse has been replaced in the squad for the this week's second Test against Pakistan after footage of the 31-year-old in handcuffs went viral

View 2 Images The ECB have confirmed that they have launched an investigation (Image: Getty Images)

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) have confirmed that Brydon Carse has been removed from the England squad for the upcoming second Test with Pakistan.

‌



The news comes just 24 hours after footage of Carse, 31, in handcuffs was shared across social media on Sunday. Carse was on a night out in Derby following Durham's County Championship win over Derbyshire, with the ECB later confirming an investigation had been launched.

‌



Reports have indicated that Carse was not formally arrested and later returned to the team hotel after being briefly detained by officers.

‌



However, the ECB released a statement on Monday outlining that the pace bowler will no longer participate in England's second Test match with Pakistan after Saturday night's incident was referred to the Cricket Regulator. He has been replaced in the squad by Sonny Baker.

English cricket hit by fresh scandal as star handcuffed after nightclub incident READ MORE :

"Following a referral from the ECB, the Cricket Regulator have confirmed that they will investigate events on Saturday night in Derby," an ECB statement read.

‌



"Brydon Carse will no longer be available for selection for the second men's Test while this investigation is ongoing and the full facts are obtained."

View 2 Images Carse was handcuffed by police in Derby on Saturday

The second Test begins on Thursday at Lords. England won by an innings in the first Test over three days at Headingley.

Article continues below

Carse has 14 Test caps and 44 white-ball appearances for his country. He featured in all five Tests in the Ashes in Australia over the winter, where he finished as England's leading wicket taker.

He took two wickets for Durham as the Division Two leaders won away against Derbyshire on Saturday.

The incident follows Ben Stokes and Gus Atkinson being stood down from England duty following a nightclub incident which occurred after the first Test win over New Zealand earlier this summer. The duo missed the second Test but would return for the third with Stokes announcing his international retirement soon after.

Sports.title: FIFA legends say 'enough is enough' as they tear into Gianni Infantino with bombshell statement
Sports.content:
FIFA legends say 'enough is enough' as they tear into Gianni Infantino with bombshell statement

Gianni Infantino has seen calls for his job as FIFA president after a highly-controversial summer, and now, a number of footballing legends have put the pressure on

View Image Gianni Infantino has been hit with criticism (Image: Getty Images)

A number of FIFA legends, including Robert Pires and Juan Sebastian Veron have said that "enough is enough," citing how football has lost core values under Gianni Infantino's leadership in a bombshell statement. The Swiss president of FIFA has come under fire following a controversial World Cup in North America, coupled with plans to sell shares of the tournament to the highest bidder.

‌



Just a matter of weeks ago, Infantino revealed plans for a scheme dubbed the FIFA Forward Enterprise, which was quickly condemned by fans of the beautiful game, as well as continental governing bodies. UEFA even went as far as boycotting world football's most prestigious tournament if Infantino's vision came to fruition.

‌



As a result, the FFE was canned altogether, with Infantino scrambling to mend broken relationships worldwide. And now, a number of footballing legends have vowed to make a difference, refusing to sit in silence as the game loses meaning.

‌



Gianni Infantino clashes with reporter with bald jibe as FIFA boss told to stay away READ MORE :

Gianni Infantino losing grip on FIFA as Ireland's FA release statement in another blow READ MORE :

In a statement shared on social media, a cohort of players wrote: "As players, football has given us everything, and we have given our lives to it. Between us, we have played on its greatest stages and worn our national shirts with pride.

"But we know that none of our achievements would’ve been possible without the fans, whose passion and commitment is the foundation of this game. We share the exact same concerns as the millions of fans around the world.

"Like them, we have watched the game we love drift away from its core values under FIFA’s current leadership. For too long, we’ve seen major decisions taken without players being consulted or considered, and without any regard for the fans who sustain the sport.

‌



"Change is necessary. Power has blurred the current leadership’s ability to distinguish between its own interests and what is best for football. Recent events have made silence impossible. Enough is enough.

Sports.title: Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street
Sports.content:
Ollie Watkins transfer saga has turned ugly - but loyalty is a two-way street

Ollie Watkins' time at Aston Villa could be up with the player supposedly choosing not to play on Sunday - but clubs and players can be equally disloyal when it suits them

View 3 Images Ollie Watkins looks to be trying to force Aston Villa's hand (Image: Molly Darlington/Getty Images)

The transfer window can be a particularly bruising time for players, egos and reputations. And there is unlikely to be too much sympathy from Aston Villa fans for Ollie Watkins after Unai Emery ’s post-match comments.

‌



Villa lose 4-0 at Brighton, the club has been left in a bit of a mess (again) by a messy transfer window which has seen big-name departures like Youri Tielemans, Ezri Konsa, Lucas Digne and Morgan Rogers with Emiliano Martinez likely to follow.

‌



So, the Watkins story - a live transfer target for Saudi Pro League club Al Hilal - certainly meant people are talking about the Villa striker rather than a humiliating defeat. A distraction tactic?

‌



It has made Watkins the villain of the piece with Emery hinting heavily - but not quite saying it out right - that the England striker refused to play at Brighton.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Watkins, 30, is being offered a huge contract in the Saudi Pro League, it would be a fantastic pay day for a player who has reached the very top in his career having really battled his way up from non-league. This is a really nice, understated but determined player who does not really seek the spotlight but there have been ups and downs at Villa.

‌



It has largely always been up when he is on the pitch because he works hard, scores goals and gives his all for the team. He has enjoyed success with the Europa League and helping the club qualify for the Champions League.

The downs have been when he has been dropped, he has been left out on numerous occasions and when players are axed from the team no-one stands up for them.

It’s just when the suggestion comes they don’t want to play for the team. Emery is such a good manager and one of the reasons is because he’s a bad loser. He’s so determined to win. As the saying goes, show me a good loser and I’ll show you a loser. Emery is a winner.

‌



View 3 Images Unai Emery didn't shy away from addressing Ollie Watkins' situation (Image: Joris Verwijst/Soccrates/Getty Images)

After the Brighton game, you could see he was fuming, Watkins was caught in the crossfire and is now public enemy No.1. It was Villa who denied Watkins a move to Arsenal in January 2025 when the Midlands club did need to sell. Arsenal will always say that it was Villa who first sounded them out. Villa eventually sold Jhon Duran to balance the books.

Watkins was priced out of a move but, like all players, is a commodity who is owned by his club - until they don’t want him. Then he’s just discarded. Villa have sold so many players this summer that it must have created some uncertainty. If you look at what happened last season - they did not win any of their first five Premier League games and scored just one goal - this transfer carousel is not new.

‌



They have been prolific buyers and sellers. And so is Watkins so wrong? There is no way a player should go on strike to force a move when they are paid so well in the first place.

View 3 Images Morgan Rogers is one of several high profile sales made by Aston Villa (Image: Darren Walsh, Chelsea FC via Getty Images)

But is it always that black and white? You can be sure players up and down the country will be talking with their clubs, agents and managers about what the future holds.

‌



Many players will feel as if they need to move on. This is not the era of player power. But we have seen a shift of more clubs openly courting transfer targets - even if they are under contract.

Every club does it and if that turns the odd head - especially when a move would be for life-changing money - then they probably are not in the right frame of mind to play.

But equally, the player will probably recall the last time they were dropped and ask their own questions about loyalty. It must be a two-way street. Clearly, Villa fans might not agree right now. But this saga has probably happened at every club this summer - but not so publicly.

Sports.title: Michael Owen admits Liverpool star is 'running out of excuses' after latest showing
Sports.content:
Michael Owen admits Liverpool star is 'running out of excuses' after latest showing

Alexander Isak led the line in Liverpool's draw at Newcastle with the Swede again underwhelming as Michael Owen insists the striker has to start producing

View 2 Images Michael Owen is running out of patience with Alexander Isak (Image: 2023 Getty Images)

Michael Owen says Alexander Isak is "starting to run out of excuses" after the Liverpool striker produced another below par performance.

‌



The Swede led the line for the Reds as they drew at Newcastle, in what was Isak's first return to St James' Park. The forward proved himself to be among the world's best strikers when he was with the Magpies, which prompted Liverpool to pay a record £125million for him.

‌



Isak endured an injury-hit first season at Anfield, which limited his involvement and meant he only scored four times. Now he's enjoyed the benefit of a pre-season ahead of his second year at Liverpool, with onlookers now adamant he has to produce.

‌



Owen was once Liverpool's main poacher and knows first hand how challenging it can be to recover from injury. However he believes time is running out to afford Isak any leeway following his latest below par showing.

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

Owen told talkSPORT: "I had plenty of injuries in my career so I know how hard it is to get back and you do need a bit of time. We’ve given him time, everyone has given him time and understood that. But he’s finished the season, then he’s gone to the World Cup and now he’s had a pre-season and you just think OK, now we’re starting to run out of excuses.

‌



"We need to see the real Isak and we know how good he is. Wow, we saw him for Newcastle and he’s absolute class. We haven’t seen it for Liverpool just yet and questions will come now. As I say, always give him the benefit of doubt in the past but at the start of this season we’re expecting.

‘Liverpool absolutely need him, they’ve lost Salah, Ekitike is out, there’s not that many options in attacking areas. They absolutely need him in top form and yesterday he was far from it, I thought he was a yard off and that’s worrying."

View 2 Images Alexander Isak struggled to have an impact in Liverpool's draw at Newcastle

‌



Cody Gakpo and Dominik Szoboszlai were the two men on target for Liverpool. Isak, who was regularly booed by the Newcastle crowd, had his best chance in the second-half, but blazed over from the edge of the area.

Isak scored 62 times in his three years at Newcastle but has never looked like replicating that form whilst at Anfield. Liverpool are looking to justify their outlay, especially with Hugo Ekitike, who cost around half Isak's fee, scoring 17 times in his debut season.

Sports.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan gives honest take on snooker future - 'There's nothing I can do'
Sports.content:
Ronnie O'Sullivan gives honest take on snooker future - 'There's nothing I can do'

Ronnie O'Sullivan is through to the last 32 of the Wuhan Open after beating Ashley Carty 5-2, but he was critical of his performance and feels powerless to do better

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan was typically candid in his assessment (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

Snooker legend Ronnie O'Sullivan has admitted that there's 'nothing he can do' to improve on his 'pretty bad' form. Despite winning his opening game at the Wuhan Open 5-2 against Ashley Carty, O'Sullivan was downbeat.

‌



The seven-time world champion made a high break of just 59 and was fortunate not to be punished by Carty, who missed a string of opportunities. O'Sullivan reckons that he hasn't been at his best for four years, with his performance against Carty coming as no surprise to him.

‌



"My performance was pretty bad really," the Rocket said. "You have to call it out. I'm not going to lie. I'm not going to try to delude myself and say there was some good stuff.

‌



"It has been pretty bad for a long time, so I expect to play pretty bad every time I go out there. I know I don't have anything to prove and that is what everyone keeps telling me.

‌



"However, for my own selfish reasons, I miss playing well and dominating the table, beating anyone who is in front of me. I miss that feeling, but there is nothing I can do about it."

O'Sullivan doesn't have long to wait until his next match, facing Chinah's Yao Pengcheng at 7am UK time on Tuesday in the last 32. His chances of making a deep run at the Wuhan Open have been boosted by Wu Yize's early exit.

The world champion suffered a shock 5-4 loss against Artemijs Zizins on Monday. Latvian youngster Zizins has been awarded a clash with Stephen Maguire at the same time slot as O'Sullivan's match.

‌



Last month, O'Sullivan revealed that he's set himself a deadline of 2028 to beat Stephen Hendry's record for World Championships. The 50-year-old is currently level with seven and told World Snooker Tour: " I'd love to win another World Championship.

Can Ronnie O'Sullivan get back to his best? Have your say in the comments section.

View 2 Images Ronnie O'Sullivan was unhappy with his display against Ashley Carty (Image: Tai Chengzhe/VCG via Getty Images)

‌



"I've got two attempts at it. Three years previous, I wasn't cueing well enough, so I feel like if I can find a bit of cueing find some form at Sheffield… if I don't do it this this season or the next season, then it'll definitely never happen.

"But I'm pleased with my career. I'm happy with how things have gone, and I just want to try and enjoy these next two years. I'll reassess it in 2028 and if things are really going well, and I've surprised myself, then maybe you can extend it but you have to be realistic. I'm definitely not going to be playing qualifiers put it that way.

"I'm not going to play qualifiers. You won't be seeing me go down to Barnsley trying to win qualifying matches and all that sort of stuff. I have to be realistic. If that happens, then obviously that's the end of my career. But hopefully, I can keep going for at least another two seasons."

Sports.title: 'Brutal, searing and punishing heat' - Babb on playing for Ireland at USA '94
Sports.content:
While none of the home nations qualified for the 1994 World Cup, the Republic of Ireland did.

It was a second successive appearance at the tournament for the Boys in Green, who were again led by 1966 World Cup winner Jack Charlton.

At Italia '90, the weather had been hot - but at USA '94, it was a different kettle of fish altogether.

The iconic image of Charlton launching an open bottle of water in the direction of Andy Townsend and Tommy Coyne always provides a reminder of that.

Image: Jack Charlton led the Republic of Ireland at Italia '90 and USA '94

He clashed with FIFA over their policy that bottles could not be thrown to the players on the pitch, so took to throwing the contents instead before FIFA later relented and allowed water bags to be thrown.

"They trust me to do what is right for them and I will continue to do it," Charlton said. "We have been right in pursuing this matter and FIFA's change of heart proves that."

Charlton was rarely seen without his white baseball cap that summer. Steve Staunton famously even wore one during the national anthem before the second group game against Mexico.

One of the players in the Ireland squad that summer was Phil Babb. The defender, then 23, had just completed his second full Premier League season at Coventry.

He made his international debut in a 0-0 friendly draw with Russia in March 1994, then played in the next four friendlies leading up to the tournament.

Image: Phil Babb played in all four of the Republic of Ireland's games at the 1994 World Cup

Nothing was set in stone, but he knew he would at least have a decent chance of being included in Charlton's 22-man squad, so started to physically prepare himself.

"A coach at Coventry asked me if I wanted to do anything specific - we ended up doing 12-minute sessions in a sauna!" Babb recalls, with a smile.

"We were doing burpees, press-ups, just trying to acclimatise to that intense heat. We did about six sessions - but I wouldn't recommend it for anyone now!

"I was a fit lad and had played pretty much all the Premier League games Coventry had played that season. I adapted to the heat pretty well, but I know some of the older lads really struggled."

Babb started alongside Paul McGrath in the heart of defence for Ireland's tournament opener at Giants Stadium in New Jersey.

Image: Ray Houghton's stunning strike earned a shock 1-0 win over Italy

That Saturday, they shocked an Italy side that featured Paolo Maldini, Franco Baresi and Roberto Baggio. John Aldridge's stunner sealed a memorable 1-0 win.

It was an achievement made all the more impressive by the fact the Azzurri went on to finish as runners-up - but also given the fact it was played in temperatures exceeding 30C.

"When we walked out onto the field, about two hours before kick-off, you could tell it was going to be absolutely roasting," he recalls.

"You could tell that straight away and we didn't stay out long. I just checked the grass to see which studs I wanted, then I went straight back in. I know some of the lads were walking around and taking the atmosphere in, but I thought: 'This is too hot'.

"I didn't go out for a warm-up with the rest of the lads, either. I stayed in the changing room. It was built for NFL, so they had a 40m sprint track. I warmed up in there and waited until we went out. It was brutal, it was searing, it was punishing.

"It affected everyone's game. You were saturated after just 10 minutes walking onto a pitch, so you had to conserve energy at the right times.

"Recovery was very basic and there was very little ball work because of the demands of the actual games and the fluids you lose. When you're that dehydrated, it's quite difficult. You want a drink, but you don't feel hungry and that is a key part of the recuperation."

Image: Babb, whose Ireland were knocked out by Dennis Bergkamp's Netherlands, joined Liverpool later that summer

Thirty-two years on from that tournament, football has evolved exponentially.

Sports science has taken on a key role in the game and, this summer, is likely to play into the way teams approach games tactically due to the heat. A slower tempo is expected in many.

Charlton was not prepared to facilitate the same in 1994, though.

"We only played one way, so if you tried to go off-piste, Jack would certainly let you know!" adds Babb.

"We had one style of play, with a lone striker. If it wasn't Tommy Coyne, it might have been Niall Quinn up there and we'd be putting long balls up to him, with either willing runners out wide or the midfield bombing on.

"That was the Irish way back then. Tommy ran tirelessly, to the point where he actually collapsed with heat exhaustion on the plane home.

"I think Jack's sports science was a barrel of Guinness in his room and he'd call the lads in and have a pint! I'm sure there's a high calorific content in that, so maybe he was ahead of his time!"

In spite of that, Babb's memories of the tournament are largely positive.

"I enjoyed it, I have to admit! I'd rather play in the searing heat than a wet Tuesday night in Hull," he says.

"I was a fit lad and it was quite easy for me playing alongside Paul McGrath, who was imperious in that tournament. I learned a lot from him and how he conserved his energy.

"I felt I got stronger because I got used to it. I guess our 0-0 draw against Norway would probably attest to the heat and the style of play.

"It all comes down to the individual. Footballers are supreme athletes now and they leave nothing to chance, so I think they'll cope a lot better than we did in the mid-90s."

The methods may have moved on since Charlton was throwing water onto the pitch, but Babb's memories from USA '94 provide a reminder this World Cup will be a battle against more than just the opposition.

Sports.title: Ogbene earns Republic of Ireland draw with Canada
Sports.content:
Chiedozie Ogbene's equaliser ensured the Republic of Ireland continued their good run of results as they drew 1-1 with World Cup co-hosts Canada in Montreal.

Canada went ahead in the 24th minute from an own goal by defender Jake O'Brien, heading a failed clearance into his own net from Stephen Eustaquio's corner.

Ireland were then awarded a penalty in the second half after Cyle Larin - who signed a two-year deal with Southampton earlier in the day - took out Jamie McGrath.

Canada goalkeeper Maxime Crepeau saved Troy Parrott's initial attempt, but Ogbene was on hand to slam home the rebound and tie the game in the 60th minute.

Image: Ireland's Jake O'Brien heads the ball into his own net

Ireland, who failed to qualify for this summer's World Cup, went close to a winner but Crepeau denied a charging run from Mason Melia late on.

The Orlando City goalkeeper missed out on the 2022 World Cup in Qatar after breaking his leg while playing in the MLS Cup final.

Canada, managed by former Leeds boss Jesse Marsch, officially open the World Cup on June 12 in Toronto against Bosnia and Herzegovina, before facing Qatar on June 18 and Switzerland on June 24.

They remain without captain Alphonso Davies, who is still nursing a hamstring injury he sustained while playing for Bayern Munich.

Sports.title: Republic of Ireland edge past Qatar in friendly as both sides end with 10
Sports.content:
Captain Nathan Collins headed the Republic of Ireland to a 1-0 friendly victory over World Cup-bound Qatar as both sides were reduced to 10 men.

Collins ensured Ireland got the better of a side managed by his former Wolves boss Julen Lopetegui with an early header.

However, just how the evening might have panned out had Jack Moylan not been dismissed as half-time approached, a sparse crowd inside the Aviva Stadium will never know.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, whose hopes of making it to the World Cup finals were dashed in heartbreaking fashion in March when they lost their play-off semi-final to the Czech Republic on penalties, were in complete control until Moylan's premature exit.

Qatar substitute Almoez Ali suffered the same fate 12 minutes from time.

Image: Jack Moylan was sent off before half-time at the Aviva Stadium

The game was played out against the backdrop of ongoing unease at the forthcoming Nations League clashes with Israel, and play was interrupted on several occasions during the first half as 'Stop the Game' protesters among a crowd of 28,981 repeatedly hurled tennis balls on to the pitch.

Ireland will now head for Montreal and their friendly against World Cup co-hosts Canada on June 6, while Qatar continue their preparations for the finals - they launch their Group B campaign against Switzerland in San Francisco on June 13 - against El Salvador in Los Angeles on the same day.

The Republic took the lead with just five minutes gone when, having been fouled by Ayoub Al-Oui wide on the left, Moylan curled the resulting free-kick on to the head of Collins, who glanced the ball effortlessly past 'keeper Mahmoud Abunada.

Image: Qatar's Almoez Ali was also sent off

There was a brief interruption after the protesters made their presence felt for the first time as Qatar's Pedro Miguel underwent treatment for injury, but once order had been restored, Troy Parrott whipped a first-time shot wide after being picked out by Seamus Coleman.

The Qataris simply could not get anywhere near Hallgrimsson's men and a mid-half drinks break did little to improve matters for the visitors with Abunada having to field Jayson Molumby's deflected 24th-minute shot from distance.

Lopetegui could not hide his frustration on the sideline and only the bravery of defender Ahmed Fathi denied Chiedozie Ogbene a second goal as he attempted to latch on to Liam Scales' header back across goal.

But the home side's night took a turn for the worse on the stroke of half-time when Northern Irish referee Jamie Robinson deemed Moylan's challenge on Jassem Gaber worthy of a red card, much to the Lincoln frontman's clear astonishment.

Image: Former Wolves and West Ham boss Julen Lopetegui is now in charge of Qatar

With defender James Abankwah having replaced Dara O'Shea at half-time, the 10 men found themselves under pressure for the first time on their return, although Coleman very nearly caught Abunada off his line with an audacious 52nd-minute attempt from the right wing.

Edmilson Junior dragged a long-range effort wide two minutes later after Molumby went down in midfield under Fathi's challenge and it took a fine 71st-minute reaction save by Caoimhin Kelleher - his first of the night - to keep out Yusuf Abdurisag's deflected shot.

However, Qatari hopes of salvation were dashed with 12 minutes remaining when Ali struck out at Molumby off the ball on several occasions and was also sent off.

Sports.title: Parrott out of luck as Republic of Ireland draw with North Macedonia
Sports.content:
Troy Parrott had two goals disallowed as the Republic of Ireland played out a stalemate against North Macedonia on the night on which they had hoped to book a trip to the World Cup finals.

Five days after their dreams came to an end for another four years in Prague, Ireland drew 0-0 with the Macedonians in a friendly encounter neither side wanted as the Czech Republic and Denmark fought for the big prize.

Even a third successive home victory for the first time since the 2015-16 campaign would have provided scant consolation for Thursday night's disappointment but Heimir Hallgrimsson's men had to make do with a disappointing draw.

AZ Alkmaar striker Parrott came closest to breaking the deadlock as 37-year-old defender Seamus Coleman received a standing ovation from a crowd of 39,560 at the Aviva Stadium when he was replaced during the second half of what could yet prove to be his final appearance for his country.

Nevertheless, the squad will reconvene for a series of friendlies at the end of the season ahead of next season's Nations League campaign and later Euro 2028 qualification having restored a measure of pride and established a momentum they hope will serve them well when they return to competitive action.

The hosts went on to the offensive from the off, although they were unable to find the final ball to allow either Parrott or Chiedozie Ogbene to threaten.

John Egan could not direct an 11th-minute corner at goal and Ogbene saw his snapshot deflected over three minutes later, but goalkeeper Caoimhin Kelleher had to parry Enis Bardhi's 21st-minute free-kick after it flicked off the defensive wall, with Bardhi volleying high over after the resulting corner had been only half-cleared.

Macedonia keeper Stole Dimitrievski saved Parrott's 23rd-minute header comfortably after Dara O'Shea and Finn Azaz had sparked a concerted attack, and Azaz failed to make the most of a free-kick two minutes later after he had been tripped just outside the penalty area.

Parrott was played into a promising position by Knight nine minutes before the break, only to miss the target by some distance.

The in-form striker - he scored his sixth goal in three games in Prague - might have done better again two minutes later after Azaz's clipped pass had caused problems for the Macedonian defence but he snatched at his attempt and fired high and wide.

Parrott twice had the ball in the net as time ran down but an offside flag stalled his celebrations on each occasion.

Ireland were unfortunate not to take the lead with 52 minutes gone when Azaz accepted Seamus Coleman's pass and found Parrott, who turned smartly before shooting against the upright.

Azaz curled an effort just wide and Tihomir Kostadinov denied Parrott a clear run on goal as the hosts began to turn the screw but it was veteran Coleman's 61st-minute departure as

Hallgrimsson made changes which attracted the biggest cheer of the night to that point.

Wholesale changes did not help the flow of the game, which rather petered out as the whistle approached, although Ireland substitute Johnny Kenny passed up a glorious opportunity to win it at the end with a weak shot at the keeper.

Sports.title: Szmodics out of hospital and 'on the mend' after collision
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland forward Sammie Szmodics has been released from hospital in Prague after being knocked unconscious during Thursday's World Cup play-off defeat by the Czech Republic.

The 24-year-old, who is currently on loan at Derby from Ipswich, was hurt in a collision with defender Stepan Chaloupek just two minutes after his introduction as an extra-time substitute at the Fortuna Arena, sparking concerned medics to rush to his aid.

Szmodics was carried from the field on a stretcher and taken straight to hospital, where Ireland head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson later revealed he would spend the night under observation.

Please use Chrome browser for a more accessible video player Danyal Khan looks back on the heartbreaking result for the Republic of Ireland who lost their World Cup qualifying play-off against Czech Republic on penalties

A Football Association of Ireland spokesperson said on Friday morning: "Sammie Szmodics was transferred to hospital yesterday having sustained a head injury during extra time of the play-off against Czechia.

"Following further tests and a period of observation, he has been safely discharged from hospital and will continue his recovery under the care of the Republic of Ireland and Derby County medical teams."

Szmodics, who Hallgrimsson confirmed would have taken a penalty in the shoot-out which Ireland ultimately lost 4-3, took to social media to express his thanks to those who had helped him.

He posted on X: "Gutted the way it ended. Fans and boys immense all evening!! Appreciate everyone's messages. And thank you to the medical staff who acted so quickly to help me. On the mend."

Collins: Ireland must build on World Cup near miss

Ireland captain Nathan Collins is confident his side have laid the foundations to qualify for future tournaments having seen hopes of reaching this summer's World Cup finals come to an end.

Collins and his team-mates were agonisingly close to the play-off final when they led the Czech Republic 2-1 in Prague on Thursday evening with just four minutes of normal time remaining.

Image: A dejected Nathan Collins and head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson

However, Czech skipper Ladislav Krejci's late equaliser took the tie to extra-time and ultimately to penalties, where the hosts prevailed 4-3 to extend Ireland's wait for a first return to the big stage since 2002.

Asked about their progression to the play-offs, which was secured by back-to-back wins over Armenia, Portugal and Hungary, Brentford defender Collins said: "I'm not seeing many positives right now because we're in the gutter.

"But what we've created, the environment created with the fans and country, has been special. That's something we need to keep growing, to get even better at.

"That can help us get better on the pitch. We can push that and get fans to more tournaments."

Ireland had hoped to return to the Aviva Stadium on Tuesday for a showdown with either Denmark or North Macedonia for a place in the finals, but the Czechs will now host the Danes, who were 4-0 winners in Copenhagen.

Instead, Heimir Hallgrimsson's side face a friendly against the Macedonians.

Collins said: "The motivation has to be the same. We've to win to keep improving as a team and country. Any game we play at home is a big game."

Sports.title: 'Pain' - Irish heartbreak as Czech Republic win on penalties
Sports.content:
Republic of Ireland's World Cup hopes were cruelly and heartbreakingly dashed as Czech Republic came from 2-0 down - to then beat them on penalties.

Heimir Hallgrimsson's side, who went two goals up after 23 minutes in Prague, were four minutes plus stoppage-time away from victory - before Wolves defender Ladislav Krejci headed in a corner to force extra-time.

Ireland were also a handful of penalties away from going through, as penalty saving expert Caomhin Kelleher saved from Mojmír Chytil in the shoot-out to give them a momentary advantage.

But Finn Azaz and Alan Browne both missed their spot kicks, allowing Patrick Schick and then Jan Kliment to win it for the hosts.

As a result, Czech Republic will go on to face Denmark on Tuesday for a spot at the World Cup - as Ireland's wait for a first World Cup appearance since 2002 goes on.

After Wales and Northern Ireland's semi-final exits, it also means England and Scotland will be the only teams from Great Britain and Ireland at the World Cup this summer.

Image: Ireland's players walk off the pitch after defeat

World Cup play-off finals - Europe Bosnia & Herzegovina vs Italy

Sweden vs Poland

Kosovo vs Turkey

Czech Republic vs Denmark

How Ireland threw away their lead

Ireland came flying out the blocks flying in Prague. Four shots in the opening ten minutes, including Nathan Collins crashing a shot off the bar from range, set the tone for a brilliant display - and they got their rewards.

A long throw caused chaos and Nathan Collins was deemed to have been caught slightly late by Vladimir Darida by VAR, who sent referee Glenn Byberg to the monitor for a review.

Troy Parrott, who else, crashed in the penalty for his sixth goal in the last three Ireland matches. And it got better for Ireland four minutes later.

Ryan Manning's corner found Dara O'Shea at the back post and his header across was cleared off the line by Vladimir Coufal - but off goalkeeper Matej Kovar and over the line.

Image: Czech Republic goalkeeper Matej Kovar scores an own goal to give Ireland a 2-0 lead

Ireland were in dreamland but a moment of Manning madness brought the Czech Republic back into it. The defender's needless tug back on Krekci - when the ball was heading out of play - was penalised by referee Byberg, with Patrick Schick pulling one back from the spot.

Ireland did, however, manage to settle the nerves down - right throughout the second half. Despite sustained Czech pressure in the second half, they barely threatened.

It was Ireland who had the better chances after the break, with Jayson Molumby striking the post and Parrott denied by a solid Kovar save at a corner. But then heartbreak struck with four minutes of normal time remaining, as Krejci bundled the ball in at the near post from a set piece.

Krejci could have even won it with the last kick of the game but scuffed his finish, as extra-time came.

Substitute Tomas Soucek missed a glorious chance for the hosts, with Adam Idah was denied a one-on-one chance by a goal-saving challenge from Stepan Chaloupek. Penalties came and the lottery fell in the hosts' favour.

Image: Jan Kliment scored the winning goal in the penalty shoot-out

Hallgrimsson confident in Ireland future despite 'pain'

Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson:

"One word is pain. I feel pain. I feel pride for the performance of the players. They gave it all. I feel gratitude for all the supporters who supported us through the whole game, even after the loss. I feel pride being a part of that group. Personally, I know all the players will feel pain now. Only pain.

"We take with us that we can play teams higher in the FIFA ranking and can punch above our weight: Portugal, Hungary and here. We can compete with these teams. We came here with three wins in a row, a long time since that happened for this national team.

"So there's growth in this squad. It's maturing. These are been the biggest game most of these players have played. That's encouraging to know we're growing. It's strange to say that after we lost today.

"I know I'm biased in this, all the statistics and metrics of the team have improved. Big games, being on the line, crunch times all the time, we've managed to go through this. It showed the resilience, character of these players, that's why I feel confident going on."

Sports.title: Wilson key for Wales, NI aim for big upset while history beckons for ROI
Sports.content:
Sky Sports assesses Thursday's 2026 World Cup play-off semi-finals as Wales host Bosnia-Herzegovina, Northern Ireland go to four-time winners Italy and the Republic of Ireland face Czech Republic in Prague.

Thursday 7.45pm: Wales vs Bosnia-Herzegovina (winner will play Italy or Northern Ireland)

Harry Wilson is not the new Gareth Bale, but he's doing the job of Bale at his best, especially for Wales.

Fans have long been excited about Wilson's natural talent, but are now seeing his influence in the Premier League on a weekly basis for Fulham. This season, he has 10 goals and six assists for club, while for country, his stats are even better with five goals and two assists in his last five games.

If Wilson starts running the show, his confidence will feed to the other players and to the home crowd, and Wales will be very difficult to stop on their own patch.

Which World Cup group would Wales be in? If Wales qualify for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Craig Bellamy wanted to create an identity for Wales when he took over as head coach. It's now clear: he wants front-foot football coupled with intensity and energy.

Bellamy doesn't always see that in international football as he finds it slower at times compared with club football, but his Wales side will not be ponderous. You could see during the qualification campaign that Wales' intensity in winning the ball back very quickly and holding possession grew. Now it's about consistently doing it.

Apart from consistency in play, there needs to be consistency in selection. Much is always made about the 'spine' of a good team, from the goalkeeper to the glory hunter! Leeds United provide a fair chunk of Wales' spine with 'keeper Karl Darlow on form and in receipt of the No.1 keeper's jersey. Joe Rodon is the rock at centre-back that success relies upon, while team-mate Ethan Ampadu's versatility means he can link anywhere between defence and midfield. Throw in one of the in-form Premier League stars, Harry Wilson, and a strong spine can take a team a long way.

Ask Bellamy if he has thought about preparing for the play-off final against either Italy or Northern Ireland and you'll get glared at. It's Bosnia, Bosnia and Bosnia. He won't entertain anything beyond Bosnia until the game is over. It's a danger, a banana skin he wants to avoid. Thinking too far ahead isn't good on this occasion.

Geraint Hughes

Thursday 7.45pm: Italy vs Northern Ireland (winner will play Wales or Bosnia-Herzegovina)

On paper, perhaps in reality, it's David vs Goliath.

Northern Ireland enjoy David vs Goliath. Once upon a time it was David (Healy) vs England and David (Healy) vs Spain.

For smaller nations there is comfort in being the underdog. A loss would be met without a major backlash, a win makes you a hero. That's how Michael O'Neill's side will approach Thursday's assignment in Bergamo against Italy.

Which World Cup group would Northern Ireland be in? If Northern Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group B with Canada, Switzerland and Qatar.

Conor Bradley and Daniel Ballard are out. Between them they represent 50 per cent of the Northern Ireland players currently plying their trade in the Premier League.

The pair's absence is as much a blow to Northern Ireland's attacking prospects as it is defensively. Ballard represents their best aerial threat from set-pieces, Bradley their most dynamic player on the ball.

And yet for some reason that only football can explain, hope remains. The four-time World Cup winners are heavy favourites but far from the Azzurri powerhouse of old.

If Northern Ireland have it their way, it's unlikely to be a pretty spectacle. But can they frustrate their hosts? 0-0 at half-time? Pounce on the sense of angst that will exist among the home support?

To call it a free hit would be to downplay the importance of the game. But Northern Ireland are free from the weight of expectation.

Daring to dream of a result that becomes instant folklore.

Michael Morrow

Thursday 7.45pm: Czech Republic vs Republic of Ireland (winner will play Denmark or North Macedonia)

Image: Republic of Ireland boss Heimir Hallgrimsson and captain Seamus Coleman spoke to the media in Prague

History beckons for the Republic of Ireland here in Prague.

Make no mistake, this will be the biggest game to date for a lot of these Irish players as they attempt to take another step to this summer's World Cup but they must get past Czech Republic to do so.

Which World Cup group would Republic of Ireland be in? If the Republic of Ireland qualified for the World Cup they would be in Group A with co-hosts Mexico, South Africa and South Korea.

Still coming off the euphoria of the incredible back-to-back wins against Portugal and Hungary last November, this is an Irish team full of confidence.

Having spoken to a few people around the Czech Republic team, those results have been noted and they are particularly worried about Irish striker Troy Parrott, who scored five goals in those two games in November - including the 96th-minute winner against Hungary.

Head coach Heimir Hallgrimsson spoke ahead of this game about one of the key aspects is visually and mentally being ready for the challenge ahead of them, he seemed as calm and confident as usual.

However his key selection dilemma is does he bring back the experienced, tried and tested players such as Seamus Coleman, Robbie Brady and Chiedoze Ogbene - all three have had limited game-time this season for a variety of injuries.

Coleman and Brady especially are the only two players in the squad who were part of Ireland's last team in a major tournament which was in 2016 - their experience could prove vital.

Image: Can Troy Parrott recreate his Irish heroics in Prague on Thursday?

Their opponents are in a state of flux.

Czech Republic have a new head coach who takes charge of his first game on Thursday, with West Ham's Tomas Soucek also being stripped of the captaincy after November's internationals having caused shockwaves in the local media - Wolves' Ladislav Krejci has replaced him.

The pressure feels like it's all on the home side which could play into Ireland's advantage as they look to take another step to qualify for this summer's World Cup - their first since 2002.

Danyal Khan
